_comment: tan-cli#664. `doctor`'s `data` values are host facts -- installed tool
versions, absolute paths, which checks even apply on this machine -- so
unlike every other entry `Bundle the envelope contract`
(.github/workflows/release.yml) folds into envelope-contract.json's
`envelopes` map, this one is not a byte golden. It pins the KEY SET
`alp-sdk-vscode` binds to (packages/alp-core/src/deps/planner.ts reads
`data.missingPrerequisites`; the debug troubleshooting panel renders
`checks[].fix` and `data.nextSteps` verbatim, alp-sdk-vscode#491) and
never a value.
Enumerated 2026-08-12 by reading the ONE place `doctor`'s envelope is
assembled -- `python/tan/commands/doctor_cmd.py`'s `doctor()` (the
`data = {...}` literal), `Check.as_dict()` (the `checks[]` shape),
`summarise()`, `next_steps()`, and `tan.core.bootstrap.reported_missing`
(the `missingPrerequisites` shape) -- not curated by hand, and cross-
checked against a real `tan doctor --format json` run. `scope` was
added by tan-cli#549 after this issue's own worked example was written
and is included here because it is really on the wire today; the
issue's proposed shape predates it and omits it.
`status` is deliberately typed a free `string`, not an enum of its
current pass/warn/fail/unknown vocabulary: every consumer already passes
it through untouched, so a status value added later must survive the
trip rather than being coerced into today's list. The same reasoning is
applied to `scope`'s `host`/`project` vocabulary (`tan.core.doctor_scope`)
even though that one IS enforced server-side (`Check.__post_init__`) --
this file's promise is the key set, not the value vocabulary.
`fix` is OMITTED (never `null`) on a `checks[]` entry that passed, is
`unknown`, or otherwise carries no remediation -- `Check.as_dict()`'s
`skip_serializing_if`-equivalent. `missingPrerequisites` is `null`,
never `[]`, when `hostPrerequisites` found nothing missing --
`reported_missing`'s own doctring: '`[]` is NEVER a value here... One
fact, one spelling.'
Renaming or dropping a key here is the same breaking wire change
`contract/README.md`'s frozen-issue-code rule describes for `issues[].code`:
bump the CLI MAJOR/MINOR, record it in CHANGELOG.md, and open the
matching alp-sdk-vscode issue.
`python/tests/conformance/test_doctor_contract_key_set.py` is the
lockstep check: it runs a real `tan doctor --format json` and asserts
every key this file declares is present (and, for `checks[]`, that no
UNDECLARED key rides along), so this file cannot drift silently from
what the command actually emits.

checks.name: string
checks.fix: string (optional -- omitted, never null, when the check has no remediation)

dataKeys.missingPrerequisites: array of {tool: string, command: string|null} entries, or null when nothing is missing
